newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's October inflation at 0.58 pct - Fipe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's October inflation at 0.58 pct - Fipe.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.58 percent in October, up from 0.07 percent in September, a Fipe official said.
The rise in October's inflation was led by clothing and food prices, particularly of meat, beans and rice, said Fipe president Juarez Rizzieri.
Clothing prices rose 0.73 percent, while food costs increased 0.64 percent.
For November, Rizzieri estimates inflation will be around 0.5 percent. He also said he predicts 1996 inflation between 10.5 percent and 11 percent.
The Fipe institute also announced the following breakdown of its weighted inflation index for the period:
- Food 0.64 pct rise in the period
- Housing 0.62 pct rise in the period
- Transportation 1.14 pct rise in the period
- Personal expenses -0.04 pct drop in the period
- Clothing 0.73 pct rise in the period
- Health care 0.32 pct rise in the period
- Education -0.13 pct drop in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
